findings.title: import hypertools permanently silences numpy divide/invalid warnings process-wide
findings.description: hypertools/_shared/helpers.py line 16 executes np.seterr(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore') at module import time. helpers is imported (mostly via star-imports) by plot, reduce, cluster, etc., so ANY 'import hypertools' flips the user's global numpy error state for the rest of their session -- their own 0-division / NaN-producing bugs are silenced. For a scientific library this can mask real numerical errors in user analysis code.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg python -c "import numpy as np; b=np.geterr(); import hypertools; a=np.geterr(); print(b); print(a); print(np.array([1.0])/np.array([0.0]))"
findings.expected: np.geterr() unchanged by importing a library; divide-by-zero in user code still warns
findings.actual: before: {'divide': 'warn', 'over': 'warn', 'under': 'ignore', 'invalid': 'warn'} / after: {'divide': 'ignore', 'over': 'warn', 'under': 'ignore', 'invalid': 'ignore'}; 1/0 produced [inf] with NO warning raised

findings.title: analyze(x, align=False) crashes although its docstring documents False as 'no alignment'
findings.description: hypertools/tools/analyze.py docstring (lines 59-65): "align : str, dict, False, or None ... If False or None, no alignment is applied (default: None)." The legacy path forwards align=False to hypertools.tools.align.align, which only special-cases None (line 74) and True (line 76); False falls through to the dispatcher and unpack_model raises. hyp.load(..., align=False) is unaffected (load guards 'is not False'), which makes analyze the odd one out. Same crash from hyp.tools.align(data, align=False).
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.analyze(np.random.rand(25,6), align=False, ndims=3)"
findings.expected: No alignment applied; reduced data returned (per docstring)
findings.actual: ValueError: unknown model: False

findings.title: hypertools/core/config.ini is not packaged: wheels ship 90 .py files only, and get_default_options() silently returns empty defaults
findings.description: pyproject.toml has [tool.setuptools.packages.find] include=['hypertools*'] but no package-data configuration and no MANIFEST.in, so the only non-.py package file (hypertools/core/config.ini) is excluded from the wheel (verified by a real 'pip wheel' build: 95 entries = 90 .py + 5 dist-info, no .ini). On any pip-installed copy, hypertools.core.get_default_options()/apply_defaults() -- public core API, 'single source of truth' per its docstring -- silently return {} for every hypertools section (configparser ignores missing files; verified by pointing at a nonexistent path). Mitigating: nothing inside hypertools currently consumes these defaults (see X7-code-org-rest-022), so only direct API users are hit. infra note: sdist contents could not be audited (python -m build not installed in the venv and installs are forbidden); the wheel was built with pip wheel --no-deps --no-build-isolation instead.
findings.repro:
cd /tmp && python -m pip wheel --no-deps --no-build-isolation -w wheelout /Users/jmanning/hypertools && unzip -l wheelout/hypertools-*.whl | grep -c '\.ini'
python -c "import hypertools.core.configurator as cfg; print(dict(cfg.get_default_options('/nonexistent/config.ini')['plot']))"
findings.expected: config.ini included in wheel; get_default_options() returns the shipped [plot]/[reduce]/[align]/[cluster] defaults on installed copies
findings.actual: wheel: 95 files, no config.ini; missing-ini [plot]: {} / [cluster]: {} -- silently empty, no exception

findings.title: Full Procrustes math implemented twice in align/procrustes.py, already diverging
findings.description: procrustes() embeds the complete algorithm as nested fit()/transform() (lines 62-195) and the SAME algorithm is re-implemented at module level as align()/xform() (lines 198-359) for the Procrustes Aligner -- near-verbatim duplicates down to the shared 'Just do silly linear system of equations ;)' and duplicated XXX comments (lines 91/264, 142/315). They have already diverged: (a) align() short-circuits identical inputs to an identity matrix (line 253); the nested fit() does not; (b) the nested transform() uses deprecated np.asmatrix/.A (lines 183-186), so EVERY procrustes() call emits PendingDeprecationWarning ('the matrix subclass is not the recommended way...'), while xform() uses '@'. One implementation should be shared.
findings.repro: python -W always -c "import numpy as np; from hypertools.align.procrustes import procrustes; procrustes(np.random.rand(10,3), np.random.rand(10,3), format_data=False)"
findings.expected: One shared implementation; no deprecation warnings on normal use
findings.actual: PendingDeprecationWarning: the matrix subclass is not the recommended way to represent matrices ... (raised twice per call); duplicate code blocks confirmed by diff (301-line unified diff of two ~150-line twins)

findings.title: hyp.align(single array) returns a 1-element list, violating its own documented return contract; internal comment about manip's return type is wrong
findings.description: align/align.py docstring (lines 312-317): returns 'The aligned data, in the same list/single-item shape as data (matching hyp.reduce/hyp.cluster/hyp.manip...)'. Real behavior: align(single 2D array) -> list of 1 ndarray, while reduce(single) -> bare ndarray, manip(single) -> DataFrame (not an ndarray, contradicting _to_arrays's comment at lines 238-241 that 'every OTHER dispatcher (reduce, cluster, manip) returns arrays too'), cluster(single) -> list of int labels. Cross-dispatcher single-input return types are inconsistent and mis-documented.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; x=np.random.rand(25,6); print(type(hyp.align(x)), type(hyp.reduce(x, ndims=3)), type(hyp.manip(x)))"
findings.expected: align(single) -> single ndarray per docstring; comment matches manip's actual return type
findings.actual: hyp.align(single array) -> <class 'list'> len 1; hyp.reduce -> ndarray; hyp.manip -> DataFrame

findings.title: Error-message quality is inconsistent across dispatchers; reduce/describe and several IO paths give cryptic or misleading errors
findings.description: cluster/align/manip/predict/impute/apply_model give exemplary errors ('unknown X model NAME; supported names: ...'). But: (1) reduce (and describe) with an unknown string neither echoes the model name nor lists supported names, and points at the pre-1.0 URL http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html (http, and a page tied to the removed hypertools.tools.reduce layout); (2) reduce's dict-spec error instructs users to put params under the 'params' key -- the LEGACY form that elsewhere triggers DeprecationWarning (canonical is 'kwargs'); (3) reduce={'model':'Bogus','kwargs':{}} raises bare KeyError: 'Bogus' (bare-string path raises ValueError -- inconsistent by path); (4) hyp.tools.align(data, align={'kwargs':{}}) raises bare KeyError: 'model' (the 1.0 dispatcher's equivalent raises a helpful ValueError); (5) hyp.load() of a 0-byte/truncated pickle raises bare EOFError ('Ran out of input') -- _load_local catches only pickle.UnpicklingError; (6) hyp.normalize(x, normalize='sideways') raises AssertionError (not ValueError) naming the internal variable 'scale_type' instead of the user's normalize= kwarg, and disappears under python -O.
findings.repro: see tested cases 'misuse battery', 'reduce dict spec missing model key', 'tools.align dict without model key', 'reduce canonical dict with unknown inner model', 'load of 0-byte pickle', 'normalize invalid value' (misuse.py / edges.py in scratch dir)
findings.expected: Uniform, actionable ValueErrors naming the offending value and the fix
findings.actual: reduce: "ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform          methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/..."; KeyError: 'Bogus'; KeyError: 'model'; EOFError: Ran out of input; AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md describes _externals/ as the vendored implementations; they are 3-line shims to the undocumented hypertools/external/
findings.description: CLAUDE.md 'External Dependencies (hypertools/_externals/)' lists ppca.py (PPCA) and srm.py (SRM) as the vendored code. In reality _externals/ppca.py and _externals/srm.py are 3-line re-export shims ('Moved to hypertools.external.* (HyperTools 1.0)'), and the real vendored code lives in hypertools/external/ (ppca.py, brainiak.py), which CLAUDE.md never mentions. Naming is also inconsistent: private '_shared' vs public-looking 'external' vs legacy '_externals'.
findings.repro: cat hypertools/_externals/ppca.py hypertools/_externals/srm.py; grep -n '_externals' CLAUDE.md
findings.expected: Checked-in project docs describe the real layout
findings.actual: _externals/ppca.py: '# Moved to hypertools.external.ppca (HyperTools 1.0). Shim preserves the old path.' (3 lines)

findings.title: impute/predict docstrings invert the canonical/legacy dict-spec terminology used everywhere else
findings.description: align/reduce/cluster/manip docstrings define {'model','args','kwargs'} as THE canonical 1.0 spec and {'model','params'} as LEGACY (deprecated, warns). impute/impute.py and predict/predict.py module+function docstrings instead present "a dict in either {'model': ..., 'params': {...}} or the fork-style {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} form" -- calling the canonical form 'fork-style' and listing the deprecated form first with no deprecation note, even though passing it DOES emit DeprecationWarning via unpack_model (verified).
findings.repro: python -W always -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; x=np.random.rand(20,5); x[3,2]=float('nan'); hyp.impute(x, model={'model':'PPCA','params':{'n_components':2}})"
findings.expected: Consistent terminology; deprecated form flagged in impute/predict docs
findings.actual: DeprecationWarning: {'model': ..., 'params': {...}} is deprecated; use {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} instead (fires despite the docstring presenting 'params' as a co-equal form)

findings.title: Cross-module helper duplication: _import_kalman_filter, _as_dataframe, _supported_names each reimplemented verbatim
findings.description: _import_kalman_filter(): predict/kalman.py:20 and impute/kalman.py:24 are identical except one word ('forecaster' vs 'imputer') in the error text. _as_dataframe(): predict/common.py:24-27 and impute/common.py:25-28 are byte-identical 4-liners. _supported_names(): trivially re-defined in manip/manip.py:33, predict/predict.py:41, impute/impute.py:33. Candidates for core/shared.py.
findings.repro: sed -n 20,30p hypertools/predict/kalman.py; sed -n 24,34p hypertools/impute/kalman.py; sed -n 24,28p hypertools/predict/common.py; sed -n 25,29p hypertools/impute/common.py
findings.expected: Shared helpers live in one place
findings.actual: Both kalman helpers: 'pykalman is required for the Kalman {forecaster|imputer}. It is normally a core hypertools dependency; ...' -- otherwise identical; _as_dataframe bodies byte-identical

findings.title: Leftover editing-instruction comments and TODO/XXX census
findings.description: reduce/reduce.py lines 154 and 221 carry '# Remove np.string_ check as it's deprecated in NumPy 2.0' -- a past edit instruction, not a description of the code. Full non-plot TODO/XXX census: align/procrustes.py:91 '# XXX check for being invariant?', :142 '# XXX with reflection False -- not sure if here or there or anywhere...', :264 '# TODO: check for being invariant?', :315 (duplicate of 142 -- both copies of the duplicated algorithm carry the same doubt). Remaining TODO in the codebase is plot/backend.py:545 (other unit). No FIXME/HACK/WIP found. Only '2.0' reference outside git history is the untracked tests/screenshots/verification_v1.0/INDEX.md ('hypertools 2.0 visual verification matrix').
findings.repro: grep -rn -E 'TODO|FIXME|XXX|HACK|WIP' hypertools --include='*.py'

findings.title: Inconsistent subpackage export surfaces; hypertools' own modules import exceptions via the back-compat shim
findings.description: Subpackage __init__ exports differ arbitrarily: align exports Aligner+pad+trim_and_pad+all aligner classes; manip exports Manipulator+all manipulators; predict exports Forecaster+resolve_t+classes; impute exports Imputer+classes; but cluster exports only cluster/models/mixture_models (no Clusterer) and reduce exports only reduce/describe (no Reducer). Separately, first-party modules import exceptions from the legacy shim path hypertools._shared.exceptions (io/sources.py:48, io/load.py:10, io/lsl.py:81, plot/backend.py:100) instead of the canonical hypertools.core.exceptions the shim points to.
findings.repro: cat hypertools/*/__init__.py; grep -rn 'from.*_shared.exceptions' hypertools --include='*.py'
findings.expected: Uniform export policy (dispatcher + base class + models); internal imports use the canonical path
findings.actual: cluster/__init__.py: 'from .cluster import cluster, models, mixture_models' (no Clusterer); reduce/__init__.py: 2 lines, no Reducer; io/sources.py:48 'from .._shared.exceptions import HypertoolsIOError'

findings.title: Dead Python<3.8 fallback in config.py; three config-named things, one of which nothing consumes
findings.description: hypertools/config.py try/excepts to 'importlib_metadata' with a '# Fallback for Python < 3.8' comment, but requires-python is >=3.10 and importlib_metadata is not a dependency (the fallback could only ever ImportError). Naming triple: hypertools/config.py (version only) vs hypertools/core/config.ini (defaults) vs hypertools/core/configurator.py (reader). And get_default_options/apply_defaults have ZERO callers inside hypertools (grep: only the core/__init__ re-export; plot/backend.py:918 'bound_args.apply_defaults()' is inspect.BoundArguments) -- the 'Central default options ... single source of truth' machinery is currently unused by the package itself (real defaults live in signatures and _shared/params.py), compounding X7-...-004/012.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'apply_defaults\|get_default_options' hypertools --include='*.py' | grep -v core/configurator.py
findings.expected: Version helper without dead branches; one live defaults mechanism
findings.actual: callers: hypertools/core/__init__.py:9 (re-export) and hypertools/plot/backend.py:918 (unrelated inspect API) only

findings.title: Procrustes(index=...) is accepted but has no effect at fit time; fitter docstring is garbled
findings.description: procrustes.py fitter() always uses data[0] as the default target (line 392-393); the index kwarg it pops is only stored for transformer-side lookups. Verified: hyp.align(data, model=Procrustes(index=2)) == hyp.align(data, model=Procrustes(index=0)) exactly. The fitter docstring both implies index picks the target ('aligned to a common target (or to data[index]/data[0] if target is None)') and contains a garbled clause ('index used to select the default target within data when target is None and data is a list of length 0 (kept for downstream lookups)'). Also transformer line 443 misuses assert with an IndexError instance as the message and the f-string is missing its closing paren: f'Index {index} is outside the range of list length ({len(proj)}'.
findings.repro: misuse2.py case H (scratch)
findings.expected: index either selects the fit target as implied, or is documented as transform-only
findings.actual: same result regardless of index: True

findings.title: Tests layout census: comprehensive coverage; only gaps are a dedicated analyze test file and describe's helper functions; skip census clean
findings.description: 83 top-level test files + 11 per-module subdirs; 1500/1502 tests collected (2 deselected via the documented 'bigdata' marker in pyproject addopts). Every top-level public API function has dedicated test files EXCEPT hyp.analyze (exercised only inside test_cross_module_kwargs.py / test_pipeline_analyze_hardening.py / others -- adequate but no tests/test_analyze.py) and reduce/describe.py's public helpers get_corr/get_cdist (no direct tests; describe() itself is tested). All skips are conditional with stated reasons (importorskip plotly/torch/datasets/gensim/pykalman/statsmodels; skipif ffmpeg/scikit-image/pylsl/fonts; CI-only guards); no unconditional @pytest.mark.skip dead tests found. tests/test_helpers.py keeps the otherwise-dead parse_args alive (X7-...-010). tests/matplotlibrc pins Agg (good); tests/data/drive_large_file_interstitial.html is a legitimate fixture.
findings.repro: pytest --collect-only -q | tail -1; grep -rn 'pytest.mark.skip|importorskip|skipif' tests --include='*.py'
findings.expected: Documented-coverage map; no dead tests
findings.actual: 1500/1502 tests collected (2 deselected) in 4.55s; skip census: all conditional (see tested-case log)
